Roast beef tenderloin in sour cream sauce - Svíčková

• • 4 lbs. beef tenderloin
  • • 3 slices bacon
  • • 1/2 cup vegetable oil
  • • 2 cups sliced soup greens (carrots, parsnips, celery root)
  • • 1 medium onion, sliced
  • • few grains allspice, whole black pepper, thyme, bay leaves, nutmeg
  • • 2 tablespoons flour
  • • 1 cup beef stock
  • • juice of one lemon
  • • 1.1/2 cups sour cream
  • • salt and pepper
Tenderloin must be aged and all the fat trimmed off. Cut small slits along the grain of the meat and stuff them with thin strips of bacon. Salt and pepper the meat and set aside.
In a large frying pan combine the oil, half of the sliced soup greens and the onion; place the roast on top and brown on all sides.
In the meantime preheat the oven to 350F. Transfer the roast and the vegetables into a roasting pan, add the remaining

vegetables and spices. Roast 40-45 minutes, basting with beef stock and juices from the pan. Remove the roast, keep it warm. Pour the pan drippings into a large stewpan, skim the fat, set pan over medium heat and deglaze, using stock or water. Add the flour, simmer five minutes. Place the roast in the sauce, add the lemon juice and simmer until the meat becomes tender on the outside (20 minutes).
Strain the sauce, discard the spices, mash the vegetables and mix them into the sauce. Blend in the sour cream and simmer for a few minutes. The sauce should be medium thick.
Slice the roast, pour some sauce over it and serve the remainder in a sauce dish.
It is important that you make enough sauce, adding beef stock and sour cream. Taste it and add
salt, pepper, lemon juice – if needed. The taste should be mildly piquant. The typical accompaniment is crouton or yeast dumplings, or noodles.

Alternative – Lard the tenderloin, grease a roasting pan with oil, cover the bottom of the pan with the vegetables, lay the roast on top, add more vegetables, spices and lemon juice. Add the remaining oil, cover and marinate overnight. Next day prepare the roast as indicated above.

▷ If planning to prepare a larger quantity, for example a whole tenderloin, increase all ingredients accordingly. Instead of browning the roast by frying, roast it on all sides in a hot oven (475F), then lower the temperature to 350F and proceed as shown above.
Beef tenderloin slices (shortcut for "svíčková") - Řezy ze svíčkové

• • 4 lbs. beef tenderloin
  • • 3 slices bacon
  • • 4 tablespoons vegetable oil
  • • 4 tablespoons butter
  • • 1 medium size onion, chopped
  • • 2 pickled cucumbers (sour), sliced
  • • 2 canned fillets of anchovies, chopped
  • • 3 teaspoons capers
  • • chopped parsley, thyme, marjoram, lemon rind
  • • 1-1/2 cups sour cream
  • • 2 tablespoons flour
  • • 1-1/2 cups chicken or beef stock, or water
  • • salt and pepper

• • 2 lbs. ground round
  • • 1 whole egg
  • • 2 hard baked rolls
  • • 2 slices bacon
  • • salt, pepper, marjoram
  • • 1 medium size onion
  • • 3/4 cup water
  • • 3/4 cup bread crumbs
  • • 1/2 cup oil for frying

Cut the tenderloin into 1" thick slices. Pound each slice with the palm of your hand and lard with half slice bacon each. Salt and pepper them lightly and fry in hot oil about 2-1/2 minutes on each side. Place them in a casserole, keep them warm.

In a saucepan combine melted butter, onion, pickles, anchovies, parsley, capers, lemon rind, marjoram and thyme and brown all. Add flour, brown a little more. Add stock or water, sour cream. Simmer for five minutes, strain and pour over the meat slices. Simmer until heated through.
Soak the rolls in water, squeeze off excess liquid, shred them. Blend them with the ground meat, egg, chopped onion, diced bacon, salt, pepper and marjoram.
Form 12 hamburgers, coat them with bread crumbs and fry on both sides.
Instead of frying, they can be roasted in the oven, basting them with hot oil, their own juices, chicken or beef stock, or water.
Serve with mashed potatoes and salad. Or serve cold with dark bread, potato salad, or pickles.
Veal chops with caraway seeds - Teleci žebirka na kminë

• • 6 veal chops
  • • 1/2 cup flour
  • • 1/2 cup vegetable oil
  • • 2 tablespoons butter
  • • 1 cup chicken stock
  • • 1 small onion
  • • 1 teaspoon caraway seeds
  • • salt

Pound the veal chops lightly-they should not be more than 1/2" thick. Make a few short cuts on the edges to prevent curling, salt them on both sides, and dust with flour on one side. Brown chops in hot oil on both sides, floured side first. In a skillet combine the butter and finely chopped onion and set over medium heat.
When the onion becomes translucent add the caraway seeds, some of the chicken stock and the veal chops and simmer about 30 minutes or until the chops are tender.

Remove the veal chops. Bring the liquid to boil, blend in flour and remaining stock, and boil until the sauce thickens (about 5 minutes). Strain the sauce over the veal chops, simmer 5 minutes. Serve with noodles, rice, salad.

• • 6 veal chops
  • • 1/2 cup flour
  • • 2 eggs
  • • 1/3 cup milk
  • • 1 cup bread crumbs
  • • 1 cup vegetable oil
  • • salt

Pound the veal chops. Make a few short cuts on the edges to prevent curling, salt them on both sides. Dip each in milk, dredge in flour shaking off excess, then dip in beaten eggs and coat with bread crumbs.
Fry in hot oil in a covered pan for 5 minutes, turn them and finish frying uncovered. Drain on paper towel. Serve with potato salad, mashed potatoes, green vegetables, salad.
Leg of lamb in wine sauce - Skopová kýta dušená

• • 3-4 lbs. lamb leg, boned, skinned (4-5 lbs. with bone)
  • • 1/3 cup vegetable oil
  • • 5 slices bacon
  • • 1/2 teaspoon each of ginger and ground nutmeg
  • • salt and pepper
  • • 1 parsnip, 3 carrots, 1 celery root,
  • • 1 medium onion
  • • 3 bay leaves, whole allspice, whole black pepper
  • • 3 tablespoons flour
  • • juice of 1 lemon
  • • 1/4 cup cranberry juice, unsweetened
  • • 1 cup dry red wine
  • • 1-2 cups chicken stock
Slice thinly parsnip, carrots, celery root and onion.
Trim off excess fat from the meat, lard it with bacon (= make small slits in roast and push a strip of bacon into each slit).
Mix salt, pepper, ginger, nutmeg. Rub over lamb.
Heat the oil in a large stewpot, add the sliced vegetables, cook five minutes.
Place the lamb in the pot, brown it lightly, sprinkle with the remaining spices.
Cover and simmer 1 hour, gradually adding chicken stock.
Spoon fat from the juices, stir in flour and cook until lightly browned.
Blend in lemon juice, cranberry juice, wine, chicken stock.
Return lamb to the mixture, cover and simmer until tender for about 1 hour.
Place lamb on a warm serving platter, garnish with mint, cranberries, snipped parsley, chestnuts.
Strain the sauce, heat thoroughly, serve in a saucedish.

  • • 4 tablespoons butter

Roast the duck in the same manner as the goose. Do not stuff with apples.
While roasting, baste often with butter.
Duckling with Madeira wine - Kachna na vině

• • 1 duckling, 5-6 lbs.
  • • 5 slices ham, cut in stripes
  • • 8 tablespoons butter
  • • 1 cup Madeira wine
  • • 1 cup chicken stock
  • • 3 tablespoons flour
  • • salt and pepper

Rinse duckling, pat dry. Sprinkle with salt and pepper inside and out. Melt butter in a roasting pan, add ham and duckling. Brown it quickly on both sides under the broiler. Lower oven temperature to 350F. Pour Madeira wine over duckling. Add some of the chicken stock, salt and pepper, and cover with buttered waxpaper. Roast 1 to 1-1/2 hours, occasionally adding the remaining chicken stock.
Salmon trout with dill sauce - Pstruh s koprovou omáčkou

• • 6 trouts, 4 lbs., cleaned, with heads and tails left on
  • • 1/2 bottle white wine
  • • 1.1/2 quarts water
  • • 1 medium onion, quartered
  • • juice of one lemon
  • • 10 black peppercorns
  • • 2 bay leaves
  • • 6 tablespoons butter
  • • parsley, finely chopped
  • • salt

• • 3 tablespoons butter and 4 tablespoons flour
  • • 2 tablespoons finely chopped dill
  • • 1 small onion, finely chopped
  • • parsley, finely chopped
  • • 2 cups fish broth
  • • 1 tablespoon vinegar
  • • 1 teaspoon sugar
  • • 1/2 cup heavy cream
  • • salt

Heat the wine, water, onion, lemon juice, bay leaves and peppercorns. Simmer 10 minutes. Add the trouts and simmer gently for 15 minutes, without boiling.

Drain fish, arrange on a heated serving platter, keep it warm. Strain the broth from the fish, reserve 2 cups for dill sauce. Meanwhile, prepare the sauce. Melt butter in a saucepan, blend in flour, stir and cook until golden. Add onion, parsley, fish broth, vinegar, sugar, salt. Cook, uncovered, until sauce thickens. Strain. Blend in the cream and chopped dill. Heat through, do not boil. Pour hot butter over trouts, garnish with parsley. Hand sauce separately.

• • 12 oz. egg noodles
  • • 8 oz. fully cooked ham slices, cut into short strips
  • • 3 eggs, separated
  • • 4 tablespoons butter
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
  • • salt
  • • 1 tablespoon butter
  • • 2 tablespoons bread crumbs.
  • • 2/3 cup heavy cream

Cook noodles in lightly salted water, drain and splash with cold water. In a bowl cream butter, egg yolks, lemon rind. Combine mixture with noodles and ham. Blend thoroughly. Fold in 3 stiffly beaten egg whites. Put into buttered and bread crumbs coated casserole. Pour the cream evenly over top and bake uncovered at 350F 35-40 minutes or until golden brown on top. Serve straight from oven, with green salad or tomato salad.

• • 6 medium size green peppers
  • • 3 tablespoons vegetable oil
  • • 1 small onion, finely chopped
  • • 1 lb. finely ground pork or beef
  • • 1 egg, whole
  • • 1/2 cup firmly cooked rice
  • • 2 tablespoons butter
  • • 2 cups tomato sauce
  • • salt
Slice stem ends from peppers, remove white fiber and seeds. Drop into boiling salted water, simmer 1 minute. Drain on a sieve or paper towel. Pat dry cavities.
Meanwhile, heat oil in a skillet, add onion and ground meat, sauté 10 minutes, mixing often. Blend in the egg, rice and salt. Spoon mixture into peppers, pressing firmly towards bottom and sides.
Arrange stuffed peppers in a flameproof buttered casserole, pour tomato sauce over all. Simmer, covered, 30-35 minutes. Serve with noodles or gnocchi.
Knead until dough is smooth and separates from the bowl. Let it rise in a warm place for 30 minutes.

Cut tablespoonfuls of dough, round them into balls, let them rise on a floured surface for 10 minutes. Drop dumplings into rapidly boiling salted water, boil 5 minutes, turn them around with a spatula and cook another 5 minutes. Drain, pierce each with fork, sprinkle with hot butter.

Optional: Coat with fried bread crumbs.
Serve with meats and sauces.

• • 5 medium potatoes
  • • 1 cup flour
  • • 1 cup cream of wheat, regular, not precooked
  • • 4 tablespoons butter
  • • 2 whole eggs
  • • salt
Peel potatoes, cook in salted water, drain. Mash them, add butter, eggs, salt. Mix thoroughly, blend in flour and cream of wheat. Knead until dough is smooth and dry.
Pinch off bits of dough, roll into 2" balls. Cook in lightly salted boiling water 10-12 minutes. Serve immediately.
Serve with roast goose, pork, cabbage, sauerkraut.

Fresh yeast is sold in most American supermarkets packed in 2 oz. cubes and dated for freshness (Fleischmann's, Red Star). Store it in the refrigerator but remove it at least 1 hour prior to using.

• - All ingredients as well as the pastry board or the mixing bowl must be at room temperature. Milk and butter must be lukewarm, not hot. It would inactivate the yeast. When the dough is set aside to rise it must be in a warm and draft free place. The dough should be dusted with a little flour and covered with cloth napkin.
  • - While kneading the dough, the melted butter and the salt should not touch directly the leavening, as this would retard fermentation. Therefore mix the salt with the flour and add the butter in the end when all ingredients are already mixed with the leavening.
  • - The dough for larger pieces is thicker than for small size pastries. If you find it difficult to use a wooden spoon, you can knead with hands after all ingredients are well mixed. The dough must be kneaded thoroughly, until it is smooth, feels dry, and no longer sticks to the bowl, spoon and hands.
  • - The quantities of ingredients indicated are to be followed exactly. So is the sequence of additions.
Sugar - unless otherwise indicated, i.e. crystal or confectioner's sugar, means granulated sugar.
Flour - means sifted flour. In the U.S. all flour is sold pre-sifted.
Grated lemon rind - If you do not have a manual grater, peel the lemon and chop the rind finely.

• • 4 cups coarse flour, Gold Medal Wondra
  • • 1 oz. fresh yeast
  • • 1-1/4 cups milk
  • • 1/2 cup sugar
  • • 4 egg yolks
  • • 6 tablespoons butter
  • • dash of salt
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
  • • 4 tablespoons butter for baking pan and brushing

• • 2 cups milk, or light cream
  • • 4 egg yolks
  • • 1/2 cup sugar
  • • 1 teaspoon vanilla sugar
  • • 1 tablespoon corn starch

• • 1 cup white table wine
  • • 1 whole egg
  • • 3 egg yolks
  • • 1/3 cup sugar
  • • 1 teaspoon vanilla sugar
  • • dash of cinnamon
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon

Prepare dough in the same manner as in Bohemian muffins. Roll it out to 1/3" thickness. Using a cookie cutter or a glass 1" in diameter cut out round cakes and lay them tightly together in a buttered baking pan. Brush sides and top with melted butter. Let rise 30 minutes in a warm place. Preheat oven to 350F, bake 20-25 minutes or until golden brown on top.
Serve warm with vanilla sauce or wine froth.

In a saucepan cream egg yolks, sugar mixed with vanilla sugar, corn starch. Gradually add hot milk or cream, stirring constantly. Set over low heat, bring to boiling, stirring steadily until desired thickness is reached. Sauce should be medium thick. Strain, serve warm.
Combine all ingredients in a saucepan. Set over low heat, beat with a wire whisk or electric mixer at low speed until mixture thickens and foams. Serve warm.

• • 2 cups flour
  • • 1/3 cup sugar mixed with 1 teaspoon vanilla sugar
  • • 1 stick butter
  • • 2 tablespoons milk
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
  • • red raspberry or red currant preserve

On a floured pastry board knead all ingredients into a ball using the palms of your hands, not the fingers. The dough will be smooth and will not crumble. You can let it rest for a few hours, overnight or more. You can use it right away also.

With a roller pin roll the dough out as thin as possible. (1/8"). Cut it into 1-1/4" round cakes, using a cookie cutter or a glass. Separate half of the round cakes and cut out a small round hole in the center, the size of a thimble. Use a cookie cutter or a thimble. Place the round cakes on a clean, dry cookie sheet and bake at 350F for 15 minutes, or until they are pink/golden. Remove from oven and cool. Before serving put 1/2 teaspoon of red raspberry or red currant seedless preserve in the center of each plain round, top it with one "holed" round. The red color is important for the look of the cookies and the sour flavor of raspberry or currant compliments them well. Unfilled cookies can be stored for weeks in an airtight container.

Stirring steadily, boil until the mixture stiffens and separates from the pan. Remove from heat. Let it cool or refrigerate overnight. Next day: Make little balls, dip each in egg white and dredge in grated chocolate. Let the "truffles" dry for 10 minutes and place them in petit-four holders.
